items.readable_text:
Content:
A one-step division equation is an equation like
[MATH: \dfrac{x}{5}=7,]
where the variable is divided by a number.

Content:
To solve a one-step division equation, we isolate the variable by reversing the operation that is applied to it.

Content:
For example, in the equation above, the variable [MATH: x] is divided by [MATH: 5.] The opposite of dividing by [MATH: 5] is multiplying by [MATH: 5.]

Content:
So, we multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: 5{:}]

Content:
[MATH: (x)/(5)|= 7; (x)/(5) × 5|= 7 × 5; x|= 35.]

Content:
This isolates the variable, so we have found the solution.

Content:
Note: We can see how multiplying by the denominator removes it from the left-hand side by swapping denominators and simplifying:

Content:
[MATH: (x)/(5) × 5|=; (x)/(1) × (5)/(5)|=; x × 1|=; x]

Content:
Recall that if the variable appears on the right-hand side [MATH: \Big(]e.g., [MATH: 7=\dfrac{x}5\Big),] you may first swap the left and right sides of the equation to get [MATH: \dfrac{x}5=7.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
A one-step division equation is an equation like
[MATH: \dfrac{x}{5}=7,]
where the variable is divided by a number.

Content:
To solve a one-step division equation, we isolate the variable by reversing the operation that is applied to it.

Content:
For example, in the equation above, the variable [MATH: x] is divided by [MATH: 5.] The opposite of dividing by [MATH: 5] is multiplying by [MATH: 5.]

Content:
So, we multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: 5{:}]

Content:
[MATH: (x)/(5)|= 7; (x)/(5) × 5|= 7 × 5; x|= 35.]

Content:
This isolates the variable, so we have found the solution.

Content:
Note: We can see how multiplying by the denominator removes it from the left-hand side by swapping denominators and simplifying:

Content:
[MATH: (x)/(5) × 5|=; (x)/(1) × (5)/(5)|=; x × 1|=; x]

Content:
Recall that if the variable appears on the right-hand side [MATH: \Big(]e.g., [MATH: 7=\dfrac{x}5\Big),] you may first swap the left and right sides of the equation to get [MATH: \dfrac{x}5=7.]
